# The Dead Simple Content Strategy For Consultants That Works

*   [Report this article](https://www.linkedin.com/uas/login?session_redirect=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.linkedin.com%2Fpulse%2Fdead-simple-content-strategy-consultants-works-boutique-marketing-c8zqf&trk=article-ssr-frontend-pulse_ellipsis-menu-semaphore-sign-in-redirect&guestReportContentType=PONCHO_ARTICLE&_f=guest-reporting)

### Boutique Growth

#### We help consultants and service providers attract better clients + charge higher fees.

Published Feb 24, 2025

[\+ Follow](https://www.linkedin.com/signup/cold-join?session_redirect=%2Fpulse%2Fdead-simple-content-strategy-consultants-works-boutique-marketing-c8zqf&trk=article-ssr-frontend-pulse_publisher-author-card)

  

Every consultant knows they need to create content. We feel the pressure to publish, to demonstrate thought leadership, to stay visible. So we sit at our desks, staring at blank screens, desperately trying to manufacture brilliant insights.

The problem? We're looking for answers in exactly the wrong place.

### The Fatal Flaw in Most Content Strategies

When I ran marketing for a boutique consulting firm, we made the same mistake most consultants make. We started by asking ourselves "What should we say?" Instead of asking "What does our market need to hear?"

The difference between these questions isn't subtle - it's the difference between content that gets ignored and content that generates real opportunities.

### Why Most Consulting Content Fails

Think about the last time you needed to hire an expert. Did you choose someone because they had the slickest presentation? The most polished videos? The fanciest production value?

Of course not.

You chose them because they demonstrated a deep understanding of your situation. They articulated challenges you thought only you faced. They showed they'd helped others overcome similar obstacles.

### The Simple Solution Hidden in Plain Sight

Last week, I spoke with a consultant who was paralyzed by content creation. She had spent six months planning her "content strategy," buying equipment, and taking courses. Total posts published? Zero.

Then we tried a different approach. I asked her to tell me about her last client conversation. She immediately launched into a fascinating discussion about why her clients keep hitting the same roadblock despite repeated attempts to solve it.

That conversation? It became her most successful LinkedIn post yet.

](https://www.linkedin.com/pulse/9-creative-ways-promote-small-business-vaughan-paynter)

### The Framework That Actually Works

Instead of starting with "What should I create?" start with:

*   What patterns do you see across client conversations?
*   Which questions keep coming up in sales calls?
*   What misconceptions do prospects consistently have?
*   Where do your clients typically get stuck?

The answers become your content calendar.

### Beyond Just Publishing

Here's what most consultants miss: Content isn't just about marketing. It's about articulating your point of view on why your market's problems persist despite their best efforts.

When you nail this, three things happen:

1.  Prospects feel deeply understood
2.  Your solution becomes the logical next step
3.  Your expertise becomes self-evident

### The Permission to Be Real

Stop trying to be a "content creator." You're a consultant. Your job isn't to entertain - it's to illuminate challenges and point toward solutions.

Your market doesn't need another polished influencer. They need an expert who can help them solve real problems.

### The Path Forward

The next time you sit down to create content, don't start with your computer. Start with your client conversations. What did you discuss this week? What insights emerged? What challenges surfaced?

That's your content. It won't be perfect, but it will be relevant. And relevance beats perfection every time.
